helpers.name: ffmpeg
helpers.description: Required command-line engine for video/audio conversion, trimming, remuxing, and frame extraction.

helpers.name: ffprobe
helpers.description: Optional companion binary for fast JSON stream inspection (falls back to ffmpeg -i automatically).

settings.label: ffmpeg executable path
settings.description: Custom ffmpeg path. Leave empty to use shared or auto-downloaded binary.

action.label: Download FFmpeg
action.description: Download standalone ffmpeg binary to shared tools directory.

settings.label: ffprobe executable path
settings.description: Optional custom ffprobe path for fast JSON media probing.

action.label: Download FFprobe
action.description: Download standalone ffprobe binary to shared tools directory.

settings.label: Default output folder
settings.description: Destination folder for finished media exports and snapshots.

settings.label: Default output container
settings.description: Initial container format selected when opening FFmpeg Studio.

settings.label: Existing file policy
settings.description: How to handle collisions when an output file with the same name already exists.

settings.label: Video preview loading
settings.description: Control when the native video player opens after selecting a file. Switch to Trim & GIF Only or Manual for even faster Convert loading.

settings.label: Timeline filmstrip thumbnails
settings.description: Generate video frame thumbnails along the Trim & Merge and GIF & Frames timeline bar in the background. Turn off for instant loading.

settings.label: Non-native preview proxy
settings.description: How to preview formats the OS player cannot decode directly (MKV, WebM, AVI, VP9, AV1). Automatic builds proxies in the background; Fast Remux skips slow 480p transcodes.

settings.label: Hardware acceleration
settings.description: Use your OS GPU decoder and encoder (VideoToolbox, D3D11VA/NVENC, QSV, AMF, VA-API) for faster filmstrips, proxies, and exports with automatic CPU fallback.

settings.label: Hardware backend
settings.description: Choose which OS hardware acceleration backend FFmpeg Studio prefers when hardware acceleration is enabled.
